toml:
# Positioning a lander on Europa: the Jovian-moon case.
#
# A lander at 20 deg north, 60 deg east on Europa's surface navigates for one Europan day
# (3.55 Earth days, the synchronous rotation period) with twelve navigation satellites at
# 4 500 km in three planes inclined 55 deg, under a 10 deg elevation mask, and a two-way
# range from Earth whenever the Earth is above the lander's horizon. Europa is tidally
# locked, so from a fixed site Jupiter never moves in the sky, while the Earth, riding
# with Jupiter, rises and sets once per Europan day: the Earth link is available only for
# part of the run, and the report shows what the local constellation must carry alone.
#
# The Europa constants (gravitational parameter, mean radius, International Astronomical
# Union (IAU) pole and prime meridian)
# are the published values cited in src/body.rs; no J2 (second zonal harmonic) is carried
# for Europa, so the relay
# orbits are two-body. The Earth-Europa light time is about 36 minutes one way at this
# epoch, near a Jupiter opposition.
#
# One simplification matters more here than at Mars: the relays orbit inside Europa's Hill
# sphere (about 13 700 km) but Jupiter's pull on them is not modelled, so their orbits are
# idealised. The run shows the geometry and what the Earth link adds (availability rises
# from about half the Europan day to about three quarters), not a flyable design.
#
# MODELLED: the constellation, the noise and the measurement model are modelling choices.
kind = "body-pnt"
body = "Europa"
epoch = "2027-02-19T00:00:00"
duration_s = 306822.0
step_s = 1800.0
seed = 11

[user]

lat_deg = 20.0
lon_deg = 60.0

[constellation]
planes = 3
sats_per_plane = 4
altitude_km = 4500.0
inclination_deg = 55.0
sigma_range_m = 1.0
mask_deg = 10.0

[earth_link]
enabled = true
